bluf: Columbia Road is an independent Helsinki digital sales consultancy of 150+ people, founded in 2016, selling ecommerce builds, customer engagement and AI powered sales to enterprise Nordic brands. The record shows no dated moves, so direction reads from the sold mix: agent implementations (Beely, Scandinavian Outdoor) and 23 LinkedIn ads pushing Salesforce agent work. The Horus read puts it Favored (+26), best placed for KJ4. A rival should know it sells CRO with no testing tool on its own homepage, lists no pricing and no partners, and 24 of its 38 recorded clients are names only, with VR Group, Oura and Aava already on other tracked books.
doing:
The positioning line, a Nordic digital sales consultancy helping companies sell better through ecommerce, customer engagement and AI powered sales, combining commercial drive with design, development, data and martech, decodes as: it builds the systems a company sells through (stores, portals, CRM and automation) and now adds AI agents to them, sold as revenue work rather than marketing. The headline claim is a client's: Nordic Finance credits it with 10x lead generation growth and reaching ambitious turnover targets.

The sold mix is 12 lines, ecommerce first. The capability read scores two lead lines at 3: Email & CRM (customer engagement flagship: CRM, marketing automation, martech stack; Fortum, Kiilto and Paulig automation cases) and Web & Product (ecommerce, the first named offer; portals, apps and stores; 60+ projects; founded as an ecommerce development consultancy). Four core lines score 2: AI Automation / Agents (roadmaps, data infrastructure, agent training; Beely and Scandinavian Outdoor agent cases), B2B & ABM (Nordic Finance 10x lead generation and Kiilto lead nurturing cases), CRO (conversion driven ecommerce design and experimentation; a Varma experimentation culture case) and Data & Measurement (one of four homepage pillars). Every media capability scores 0; SEO and AI search score 1. The one proprietary item listed is the Digital Business Toolkit. The record lists no partners.

AI posture in plain terms: it sells AI powered sales transformation, AI roadmaps, data readiness, change management and implemented agents, including multi agent builds and Salesforce agent work. The record lists no moves, no news, no jobs and no pricing signals; the status note says case pages were modified through Sep 2026. Conspicuously absent for a consultancy with a growth and marketing line: no paid media of any kind, no content or PR line, and no named technology partners despite Salesforce agent work and a HubSpot stack of its own.
clients:
Columbia Road serves enterprise clients from Helsinki, Finland, its only listed office; the prominence note names SAS, Oura, Posti, Elisa, Fortum, VR Group, F-Secure and Alko as the roster's major Nordic brands. Verticals listed run from retail and energy to healthcare and public sector.

The record holds 38 clients, 14 with an observed need and 24 names only. The mix reads CRM and owned audiences first (N6, share 0.204), then commerce and marketplaces (N7, 0.194), local and lead generation (N10, 0.175), web build and platform (N4, 0.175), AI and automation (N9, 0.165) and B2B pipeline (N11, 0.087). The signals: Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) came for CRM (digital loyalty services); Fortum for CRM and AI (growth driven marketing automation); Paulig for B2B, CRM and commerce (b2b ecommerce automation); Kiilto for leads, CRM and AI (lead nurturing with marketing automation); Nordic Finance for leads and B2B (10x lead generation growth, b2b leasing); Framery for leads (a lead to order platform); Elisa, Oura and Posti for commerce (ecommerce platforms and online sales); Beely and Scandinavian Outdoor for AI (multi agent architecture, ai agents); Helkama-Auto (Škoda) for web and CRM (a loyalty app); Almada Label and Alko for web (centralised shopify solution, mobile app).

Names only include Varma, Vaisala, Qt Group, Kotipizza and HSL; the need there is inferred from what it leads with, ecommerce builds and CRM.

Shared: VR Group also sits on the books of iprospect and embryo, Oura on instrument, and Aava on peak-ace.

What the base needs next: the Horus read ties it to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out). It is likely, moderate confidence, that the loyalty and automation clients (SAS, Fortum, Kiilto, Paulig) next buy agent work on the CRM stacks it built.
house: Say and do: 1 of 2 tested lines is practised on its own house. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: it runs its own LinkedIn ads (23). CRO is contradicted: it sells CRO and no testing tool is detected on its own homepage. No llms.txt; no AI crawlers blocked. The sitemap lists 512 URLs, 36 updated in 90 days and 53 in 365 days, with 1 AI URL counted: steady publishing, little of it about AI. Tag stack gtm and hubspot; CMS HubSpot CMS; no social pixels, test tools or ABM stack detected. Google Ads Transparency Center: the check was blocked, so its Google ad presence is unread. LinkedIn: active, 23 ads, 21 company page and 2 thought leader ads by staff; samples: 'Everyone's talking about AI agents. But what does it really look like to implement one in the Salesforce ecosystem?' and 'Used by teams at Google, H&M and Amazon. Downloaded 100,000+ times.' Meta and TikTok: no record.
market:
The Horus read gives a tailwind index of 25.7, band Favored, verdict Favored (+26), with no headwind judgment listed. Best placed for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net 0.492), driven by Data & Measurement (+2), Email & CRM (+1) and AI Automation / Agents (+1), and for KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out, net 0.211). Best scenario fit: The Commons Rebuilt (47/100); resilience 34.9; say and do integrity 50. Moves: making P7, partial on P1 (no audited AI visibility product) and P6, absent on P2, unknown on P5; P3, P4 and P8 do not apply.

The Monsoon read gives index 51.5, band Breeze, inferred. Migration 54.0 edges displacement 49.0: the hours are movable before the book is price driven, and the enterprise icp term scores -5. Web & Product (17) and Email & CRM (9) carry the most movable hours; no hub office and no onshore claim is listed, so the footprint is inferred, with a shore split of 50% South and Southeast Asia and 40% Eastern Europe.
openings: It is very likely (high confidence) that the CRO contradiction is the one to lead with: it sells conversion driven design and experimentation, cites a Varma experimentation culture case, and runs no testing tool on its own homepage; a rival that shows its own live test stack wins that comparison in the room. The falsifier is a testing tool appearing on columbiaroad.com at the next compile. It is likely (moderate confidence) that the ecommerce names, Oura, Elisa, Posti and Almada Label, are contestable on feeds, schema and entity work, which the read marks absent (P2) on a lead web line. It is likely (moderate confidence) that a transparent, outcome priced offer undercuts it, since the record lists no pricing model; the headline claim is a client's 10x figure, not a price. VR Group (also on iprospect and embryo), Oura (instrument) and Aava (peak-ace) already buy from other tracked agencies and are the names to approach. It is unlikely that an offshore price pitch moves the book, with displacement 49.0 and an enterprise icp, but 24 of 38 names carry no described work, so the question for those clients is what it actually built.
watch: I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt-out rates (December 2026 to January 2027): disclosed AI checkout GMV would strengthen the KJ4 tailwind behind its ecommerce and agent lines, and high Shopify opt-out rates would slow it.
I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures (October 2026): output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would raise the cost of its pricing silence under KJ6.

Follow up the case pages the status note says were modified through Sep 2026 and the 23 LinkedIn ads running at the Sept 2026 check; a new agent case or a testing tool on the homepage would change the CRO and P6 reads.
The next Radar compile after 2026-09-28 refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients, and may unblock the Google Ads Transparency Center read; this dossier is only as fresh as that date.
